purpose: NEAR-MISS REPRESENTATIONS THAT MUST BE REFUSED. Each case is the valid fixture with one field rewritten into a spelling that denotes the SAME session but serializes to different canonical bytes, or into a shape the producer can emit but the receipt cannot carry. Every one of these was accepted by the 1.0 draft, which is how the anchored digest stopped being a function of the session: two honest assemblers reading the same database could each produce a schema-valid receipt and anchor different digests, and receipt_id uniqueness is enforced on session_id+subject_id rather than on the payload, so the second attempt is rejected while the first digest stands. `patch` maps a JSON pointer to its replacement value; a null value deletes the field.

cases.name: session_id in uppercase hex
cases.why: The same UUID, different bytes, different digest. Exactly one spelling is admitted.

cases.name: prompt_hash in uppercase hex
cases.why: hash32 admits lowercase only, for the same reason session_id does.

cases.name: inputs_digest in mixed-case hex
cases.why: Mixed case is the shape a hand-assembled or copy-pasted digest actually takes.

cases.name: created_at with millisecond precision
cases.why: THE MOST LIKELY PRODUCER OUTPUT: pg timestamptz -> JS Date -> toISOString(). Refused here so the assembler is forced to truncate rather than emit a second byte sequence for one instant.

cases.name: created_at with a numeric UTC offset
cases.why: RFC 3339 says this is the same instant. The canonical bytes say it is a different receipt.

cases.name: created_at with a lowercase z
cases.why: RFC 3339 admits either case for the zone designator; schema 1.0 admits one.

cases.name: analyst_signature member_id in uppercase
cases.why: member_id is case-pinned so that code-point order, UTF-8 byte order and a UTF-16 sort cannot disagree about analyst_signature_order.

cases.name: weights carrying three buckets
cases.why: meanTakeWeights() unions whatever buckets the takes carried, so a three-bucket vector is producible and publicly served. The receipt refuses it rather than silently omitting weights and contradicting the session API.

cases.name: judge.source omitted
cases.why: A receipt that cannot say whether its prose was model-authored or template-authored is not attributable to what produced it, which is the property this phase exists to establish.
